note:
targetCpaCad is a published benchmark, not a measured value. Puchica has never observed its own CPA: 14,549 sessions across 90 days produced two orders, both owner tests. Replace this figure with a measured cost per purchase as soon as a paid traffic test produces one, and drop the benchmark source list when that happens.

2026-09-13: the lighting cohort is classified `lighting` - HS 9405.11.00 / 9405.19.00, 7% MFN. Carried forward otherwise unchanged from the 2026-08-24 benchmark: the CA$42 target CPA, the 30% required profit share and the 0.15 assessment probability are all still that day's measurements and are NOT re-measured here. Only the duty classification of four new handles is added, which is a lookup rather than a reading. The CPA figure in particular predates the lighting category entirely and should be re-measured against it before any paid spend - a travel-goods CPA is not evidence about lamps.
sources: Meta ads CPA benchmarks by industry 2026: median ecommerce CPA US$29.99 for the Lifestyle & Boutique band, the cheapest ecommerce category. US$29.99 x 1.40 = CA$41.99, rounded to CA$42. https://www.get-ryze.ai/blog/meta-ads-cpa-benchmarks-by-industry-2026

Meta ads CPM/CPC benchmarks by country 2026: Canada is a Tier-1 market, CPM US$14.03, with a 12% year-over-year increase in ad cost. https://www.adamigo.ai/blog/meta-ads-cpm-cpc-benchmarks-by-country-2026

assessmentProbability is an estimate, not an observation. No Puchica parcel has ever been delivered to a genuine customer, so the rate at which CBSA assesses these parcels is unknown. 0.15 is deliberately conservative against the de facto observation that low-declared-value Cainiao parcels usually clear unassessed.
Duty classification only: HS 9405.11.00 / 9405.19.00 MFN 7%, added 2026-09-13 with the switch to the Canadian market. No CPA or conversion figure was re-measured.
